title: Vite can be embedded by a CLI
claim: Vite exposes a programmatic createServer API; a Node process can configure root/port, call listen, print URLs, and bind CLI shortcuts.
evidence: The docs show createServer({ configFile: false, root, server: { port } }), await server.listen(), server.printUrls(), and server.bindCLIShortcuts().
relevance: Supports a dashboard CLI that starts a local dev server in repository development while serving built assets in installed mode.

title: React Flow fits interactive topic graphs
claim: React Flow renders interactive node/edge canvases and includes MiniMap, Controls, Background, custom node/edge types, and fitView support.
evidence: The overview example imports ReactFlow, MiniMap, Controls, Background, useNodesState, useEdgesState, custom nodeTypes/edgeTypes, and fitView.
relevance: Supports the proposed full graph view for map/fact/plan/ADR relationships.

title: Shiki provides VS Code-style highlighting
claim: Shiki can turn code into highlighted HTML with themes and can integrate with Markdown-It, including light/dark themes and transformers.
evidence: The docs show codeToHtml(code, { lang, theme }) and @shikijs/markdown-it configured with light/dark themes and transformerNotationDiff().
relevance: Supports an accurate lightweight code viewer and rendered Markdown code blocks without a full Monaco editor dependency by default.

title: jsonl-graph uses id/from/to records
claim: jsonl-graph treats nodes as JSONL records with id and edges as records with from and to; its README emphasizes jq-friendly JSONL graph pipelines and currently Graphviz rendering.
evidence: The README states 'Node has id. Edge has from and to' and 'Currently only Graphviz is supported.'
relevance: Matches Cartographer's existing JSONL graph artifacts and informs graph export/import affordances.

title: Pi skills are packaged Markdown capabilities
claim: Pi skills are self-contained Markdown capability packages with frontmatter, optional helper scripts, and command invocation through /skill:name.
evidence: The Pi skills docs describe SKILL.md structure, frontmatter, helper scripts, and /skill commands.
relevance: Supports adding a dashboard skill that starts the installed CLI for the user.

title: Pi packages can ship skills and dependencies
claim: Pi packages can declare skills, extensions, prompts, and themes under package.json pi, and npm/git installs run npm install for dependencies.
evidence: The Pi package docs show pi manifest resource arrays and dependency installation behavior.
relevance: Supports shipping dashboard frontend/server dependencies and a new skill in the existing package.

title: Cartographer stores topic planning artifacts
claim: Cartographer topics can contain proposal.md, plan.md, map/fact JSONL, plan graph JSONL, receipts, and context packs under .plan/<topic>/.
evidence: The README lists proposal, plan, map.nodes/edges, facts.nodes/edges, plan.nodes/edges, receipts, and context-packs artifacts.
relevance: Defines the dashboard's primary filesystem data model.

title: Existing workflow metrics are computable
claim: workflow_benchmark.py computes topic metrics from phase nodes, receipts, validation receipts, context packs, commands, and optional session summary data.
evidence: The helper returns phase_count, receipt_count, validation_receipt_count, passed/failed/skipped/timeout receipt counts, coverage, output estimate, and session summary fields.
relevance: Provides a reusable starting point for overview and implementation metrics.

title: ADR graph helpers are local data sources
claim: adr_records.py defines ADR directory candidates, ADR graph filenames, status/edge taxonomies, currentness, and validation behavior.
evidence: The helper defines ADR_GRAPH_DIR, adr.nodes.jsonl/adr.edges.jsonl, ADR statuses, edge types, required fields, and validation helpers.
relevance: Supports dashboard ADR metrics and ADR relationship exploration without inventing another schema.

title: Taste profile requires tactile dark UI
claim: The requested design should default to dark UI, tactile material depth, clear affordances, immediate feedback, purposeful motion, and color as wayfinding while avoiding flat generic SaaS aesthetics.
evidence: The taste profile explicitly prefers dark mode, modern skeuomorphism/tactile UI, visible depth cues, immediate feedback, purposeful motion, and functional color categories.
relevance: Defines the dashboard's visual and interaction quality bar.

title: Planning validators understand lifecycle and citations
claim: manage_jsonl.ts validates fact citations, lifecycle states, JSONL object records, supported_by edges, and private path safety.
evidence: The helper defines FACT_CITATION_RE, LIFECYCLE_STATES, JSONL parse/upsert utilities, citation support checks, and private-path safeguards.
relevance: Dashboard linkification and health checks should mirror existing validator semantics.

title: Pi extensions support command and tool UX
claim: Pi extensions can register commands and tools, interact with users through ctx.ui, and expose custom rendering, but a dashboard-start skill can avoid needing a new extension by invoking a packaged CLI.
evidence: The docs show pi.registerCommand, pi.registerTool, ctx.ui.notify/select/confirm, custom UI, and package resource loading.
relevance: Helps choose the minimal package surface: a skill plus installed CLI first, extension command later only if needed.

title: shadcn/ui fits the React component layer
claim: shadcn/ui provides accessible, customizable React components as open code built with TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and Radix UI primitives, and supports Vite projects through its CLI and component add workflow.
evidence: The docs describe shadcn/ui as accessible open-code components built with TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and Radix UI, show Vite initialization, and show adding components such as button, card, and dialog with the CLI.
relevance: Defines the dashboard's reusable React component foundation.

evidence: The Tailwind docs show configuring Vite with @tailwindcss/vite and importing Tailwind from CSS; the docs describe utility-class styling behavior.

title: ESLint flat config is the current linting baseline
claim: ESLint v9 uses flat config files such as eslint.config.js and imports core recommended rules from @eslint/js instead of legacy string configs.
evidence: ESLint docs describe flat config as the current/default configuration format and show importing @eslint/js recommended configs in eslint.config.js.
relevance: Defines the repository lint configuration foundation before adding substantial TypeScript dashboard code.

title: typescript-eslint enables type-aware TS linting
claim: typescript-eslint supports ESLint flat config and typed linting through recommended type-checked configs with parserOptions.projectService enabled.
evidence: typescript-eslint docs show flat config with @eslint/js, typescript-eslint recommendedTypeChecked configs, and projectService: true for typed linting.
relevance: Supports a stronger TypeScript lint baseline for CLI, server, client, and tests.

title: Prettier provides repository formatting checks
claim: Prettier can enforce formatting through CLI scripts such as prettier . --check and apply formatting with prettier . --write across supported project files.
evidence: Prettier docs show prettier . --check for validation and prettier . --write for formatting files in-place.
relevance: Supports consistent formatting before heavy TypeScript/React work increases code volume.

title: Hono selected for dashboard server
claim: The local dashboard should use Hono on Node.js for the read-only API and runtime asset server because it is small, TypeScript-friendly, supports modular routes, static file serving through the Node adapter, and documented SSE/streaming patterns.
evidence: Hono docs show modular app.route routing, Node static file serving via @hono/node-server/serve-static, and streamSSE usage for Server-Sent Events; user selected Hono as the preferred HTTP stack.
relevance: Resolves the runtime HTTP library open question for the dashboard server and live reload endpoint.

evidence: User selected the strict full-repo rollout option after reviewing ESLint flat config, typescript-eslint typed linting, and Prettier CLI options.
